name: custom-empty-api-key
purpose: CUSTOM with NO api_key_custom secret stored -- the state of a user who configured a local or keyless endpoint (Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio), which the custom source exists to serve. Pinned builds the header UNCONDITIONALLY: `'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + apiKey` (src/endpoints/backends/chat-completions.js:933), with apiKey from readSecret (:2396) being undefined when nothing is stored. So the expected wire form is an Authorization header that is PRESENT and equal to 'Bearer ' with a trailing space -- not an absent header, and not 'Bearer undefined'. The three outcomes are distinguishable at the recorded peer and are exactly the reason this scenario exists: an implementation that omitted the header when the key was empty would be 'safer' than pinned and would still work against a keyless endpoint, so nothing but a byte recording can catch it.
stage1Boundary: Stage 1 validates the backend -> provider transformation only. Browser-side prompt assembly happens in the frontend before the request reaches the route and is NOT covered here; a green provider-wire capture is not evidence of preset-level equivalence.

tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend.
tier2.harnessSource: tools/mock-provider/main.go: --port 0 asks the kernel for a free port, so the authority is not stable

tier2.rule: value replaced with Bearer <redacted>, presence and scheme preserved
tier2.reason: There is NO stored key in this scenario, so the value is the literal 'Bearer ' with nothing after it (chat-completions.js:933 concatenates unconditionally). The VALUE carries no secret, but it is a credential-shaped header and the recording harness refuses to commit one that normalisation has not rewritten (probe-provider-wire.mjs:503-518) -- so the rule is declared for the same reason it is declared elsewhere: the CONTRACT here is presence plus scheme, and the empty remainder is the property under test, which the guard's shape-preserving rewrite keeps visible.

tier2.rule: the mock authority is replaced with <mock> before hashing
tier2.reason: The mock listens on an ephemeral loopback port, so the authority is not a property of either backend. The rest of the body is compared byte for byte through the digest.

tier3.reason: It is a measurement of elapsed wall-clock time, so it differs on every run and no backend can match it; the value is a duration, not a contract.
